properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Valleys
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 13 at 4:57AM PDT until October 14 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical. Dangerous conditions are
forecast along the shoreline. Hazards include sneaker waves,
strong rip currents, and large breaking waves.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.90 ft MLLW) at
1:14 PM Tuesday 10/13, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.72 ft MLLW)
at 1:46 PM Wednesday 10/14. These predictions include up to
1.0 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 4 PM PDT WEDNESDAY

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 13 at 3:48AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Observations around the Northern Interior have shown areas of
mist, flurries and drizzle with temperatures around freezing.
With any mist or drizzle Tuesday morning, there is the potential
for patchy ice to develop resulting in slick conditions. Please
use caution if you are out and about this morning. The risk for
patchy ice will end this afternoon as temperatures rise above
freezing in most spots.

properties.headline: Frost Advisory issued October 13 at 4:39AM PDT until October 13 at 8:00AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures as low as 33 to 36 will result in frost
formation.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest and west central Oregon and southwest
Washington.

* WHEN...Until 8 AM PDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender outdoor plants from the cold.
Consider temporarily moving outdoor potted plants indoors if they are
sensitive to cold temperatures.

Consider temporarily covering sensitive plants with a lightweight
cotton fabric (i.e., bedsheets, thin blankets), as this will help
retain heat and provide frost protection for your plants.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; North Central
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 13 at 7:35AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
At 735 AM AST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Dorado, moving west at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.
properties.instruction:
Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

NWSheadline: A STRONG THUNDERSTORM WILL IMPACT VEGA ALTA...DORADO...TOA BAJA, MANATI AND VEGA BAJA COUNTIES UNTIL 830 AM AST
